title.purpose: Page-level h1, e.g. dashboard greeting, workspace headers.

body.purpose: Default running UI text; the base font size for the whole app.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-labels: table column headers, small captions.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for cards/panels on the canvas.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Hover elevation for cards; resting elevation for floating layers (dropdowns, popovers, avatar menu).

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Modal/dialog content only — the system's single highest elevation.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/press transition for nav items, buttons, rows.

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 550; font-size: 13px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #3575b0; color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2a5e8e; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3575b0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; color: #16202c; border: 1px solid #dde1e7; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-weight: 550; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #eef0f3; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Signature component — the single source of truth for order/work-order status color, keyed off a closed 7-family vocabulary.
components.css: .ds-status-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; border-width: 1px; border-style: solid; padding: 2px 8px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 550; } .ds-status-neutral { background: #eef0f3; border-color: #dde1e7; color: #38424f; } .ds-status-info { background: #e8f1fb; border-color: #b5cfea; color: #20496e; } .ds-status-success { background: #e8f7ee; border-color: #a3d9b6; color: #1e6b40; } .ds-status-warning { background: #fdf4e3; border-color: #f9e2b1; color: #7a5200; } .ds-status-danger { background: #fdecea; border-color: #f5b8b3; color: #8b1a14; } .ds-status-urgent { background: #fce8fb; border-color: #e6b0e3; color: #6b1466; } .ds-status-completed { background: #eeebf8; border-color: #ccc4ee; color: #3d2e8c; }

components.name: Text Input
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #dde1e7; background: #ffffff; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 13px; color: #16202c; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #647080; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #3575b0; }

components.name: Stat Card
components.description: Dashboard summary card; flat at rest, raises on hover.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid #eef0f3; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 2px 6px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08), 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04); } .ds-card-value { font-size: 29px; font-weight: 800; color: #16202c; } .ds-card-label { font-size: 13px; color: #647080; }

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: List-item and attestation checkbox (distinct from settings Toggle).
components.css: .ds-checkbox { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #c4cad4; } .ds-checkbox-checked { background: #3575b0; border-color: #3575b0; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Tab
components.description: Underline-style tab, active state in brand blue.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: inline-flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; border-bottom: 1px solid #dde1e7; } .ds-tab { background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 550; color: #647080; cursor: pointer; margin-bottom: -1px; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #16202c; } .ds-tab-active { border-bottom-color: #3575b0; color: #3575b0; }

narrative.overview: OrderHub reads like an accounting-grade ledger for a manufacturing floor: every order is a line to be tracked, matched, and reconciled as it moves from submission through cutting, QC, invoicing, and release. Steel-blue and cool-grey carry the structural weight — panels, borders, body text — while a single warm amber accent marks what currently needs a human's attention (an overdue stat, an expedited order, a hover state). The system stays flat and quiet at rest; elevation only appears as a response to interaction (hover, an open dropdown, a modal), never as decoration. Status is color-coded through one small, closed vocabulary of seven pill-shaped families reused everywhere rather than invented per screen. This is an Operate-mode surface: internal coordinators, production staff, and accounting live in it for hours, and external customers use it to place and track orders. Scanability and consistency outrank expression; personality lives in small, precise details rather than in bold color or motion.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default; shadow is a state response, not a resting decoration.
One closed status-color vocabulary (7 families) reused for every badge, pill, and row accent — never a one-off color pairing.
Amber is rare and load-bearing: it always means "this needs attention," never decoration.
Dense, left-aligned data (tables, stat rows, list rows) over illustrative or marketing-style layout.
No custom display typeface — the system typeface stack throughout, differentiated by weight and size, not by font family.

rules.name: The One Warm Voice Rule
rules.body: Amber is the system's only warm color and its only "look here" signal. It never shares a screen role with a structural color.

rules.name: The Closed Status Palette Rule
rules.body: Every status indicator maps through exactly seven named families — neutral · info · success · warning · danger · urgent · completed — each with a fixed bg/border/text triplet, light and dark. A new status must be assigned to one of these seven, never given a bespoke pair.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Family Rule
rules.body: Every level of hierarchy is expressed by resizing/reweighting one typeface, never by switching families.

rules.name: The Elevation-As-Response Rule
rules.body: A surface's shadow level should describe why it's raised (floating over content vs. blocking all content), not how important it is.

dos: Do route every status indicator through the 7-family status vocabulary — never hardcode a one-off status color.
Do keep amber exclusively for "needs attention" signals; if a new element is purely structural, use blue/grey.
Do use shadow-sm → shadow-md as the resting → hover pattern for cards, and reserve shadow-lg for modal-level content only.
Do use the pill radius only for badges, avatars, and count bubbles — buttons and inputs stay at radius-md.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface or a decorative display font — hierarchy comes from weight/size on the one system stack.
Don't treat this palette as final. It is a working placeholder and the product owner has explicitly not committed to it — expect a dedicated redesign pass.
Don't add shadow to static, non-interactive, non-layered content — it breaks the flat-by-default read established throughout the shell.
Don't reuse danger (red) for expedited/urgent orders, or vice versa — they are deliberately separate families.
